first-interaction.text: If the player has never trapped goats before:

steps.npc: Ah, what'm'ah gonna do with these damn goats...

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.npc: Hrm... ye are an outsider... but ye do have a look about ye. Tell me, d'y'ave experience herdin' goats?

steps.text: If the player has not yet completed Sheep Herder:

steps.npc: Ah, a damn shame. If ye get some experience under yer belt, come back, but these goats aren't for the weak handed.

steps.text: You need to have completed the Sheep Herder quest to hunt goats.
If the player has completed Sheep Herder:

steps.player: I have experience herding sheep, if that counts for anything?

steps.npc: Aye? Well, I s'pose I should take what I can get. Feel like helpin' out with the goat problem?

steps.player: How can goats be a problem?

steps.npc: When there's too bleedin' many of 'em!

As yer can see, on this hill, there's a... large goat herd. We think the wyrms used to eat 'em and keep the numbers down, but since we moved in, we think they've just kept spawnin' and... well, you can see what happens.
Best plan o' action we came up with is the goat pit. It ain't pretty, but the goats are dumb enough for it t'work.

steps.player: So how does goat herding come into this?

steps.npc: You herd the goats into the pit and they're dumb enough t' jump right in.
There's a pile o' spikes right 'ere. You'll wanna grab yerself a set of them and line the pit with 'em first.
The other pile 'ere is a bunch o' cattleprods. You can use one of them, or if ye fancy yerself one of them mages, me pal Jeff reckons ye might be able to pull 'em around wit' a spell or two.
Telly knee rectric grab? Dark le hure? I don't remember. If those names mean anything to ye, don't tell me. I'm better off not knowing.

steps.player: So I just prod the goats into the pit?

steps.npc: Aye, but the pit can only hold so many goats at a time. I reckon ye could fit more in if ye get better at animal handlin', but ye'd need to inspect the pit to tell, I reckon.
Once ye've got goats in t'pit, ye'll need t'sort out the carcasses. Feel free t'keep any horns or fur ye can salvage. Just remember t'line the pit with spikes again once yer done.

steps.player: So, line the pit with spikes, herd the goats into the pit, sort the carcasses and repeat. Got it, thank you!

steps.npc: Aye, ye could reduce me speech into a single line, ye bloody outsider...

first-interaction.text: If the player has trapped goats before first speaking to Geoff:

steps.npc: Have ye been pittin me goats without permission?!

steps.player: Sorry, I didn't realise that I-

steps.npc: Ha! I'm just pullin' yer leg, outsider. Ye've got nothin' t'worry 'bout!
Glad t'see ye've figured out how t'use the pit, at least. If ye need help with anythin' else, we can talk later, else I'll leave ye to it.

subsequent-conversations.player: What am I meant to be doing here?

subsequent-conversations.npc: Ye wanna grab a set of spikes from this pile o'er 'ere and line the pit wit' 'em.
Then take a prod and shove the goats in t'pit. Me pal reckons you could use a 'telly knee rectric grab' or a 'dark le hure' to do it, but I don't go fer that magic nonsense.
Ye can probably fit more goats in t'pit if ye get better at herdin' animals, but eventually it'll get full regardless.
Once it is, ye'll need to sort the carcasses. Ye can keep any furs or horns ye salvage as ye clear 'em out. Then ye can just re-line the pit and keep at it.
